Definition: middle voice of apparently a prolonged form of an obsolete primary (compare G3735); to stretch oneself, i.e. reach out after (long for):--covet after, desire.
BiblicalUsage: To reach out after something is to desire it. Paul says if a man desires the office of a bishop he desires a good work, and Hebrews says the fathers of faith desired a better country, that is, a heavenly one.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe desire shows what a heart is set on: desiring the work of a bishop is good, and desiring a better country is better still.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
